speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; could you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if the pain is constant or comes and goes?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a traumatic injury from a sudden pull; did you notice any "squaring" or box-like deformity of the finger, or is there significant difficulty extending it? Also, did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigger Finger (Stenosing Tenosynovitis) of the Right Ring Finger.

The history of a traumatic pull combined with the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the finger resting in extension is highly characteristic of flexor tendon entrapment. Would you agree to have me order an ultrasound of the finger to confirm tendon thickening and sheath inflammation?

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
